title: Google Chrome is done warning you about insecure websites after the fact
summary: The browser will now give you a heads-up before you visit an insecure website.
body: TL;DR Google is enabling Chrome’s “Always Use Secure Connections” setting for all users by default. Chrome will now warn users before connecting to insecure HTTP websites, giving them a chance to back out. Chrome won’t repeatedly warn users about approved HTTP sites, and Google says most users are unlikely to encounter these warnings anyway. An optional Chrome toggle that was first introduced back in 2022 is now being automatically enabled for everyone. Last year, Google announced its intention to make Chrome much safer for everyone , saying it would do so by prioritizing secure HTTPS connections when browsing the web and by warning users about websites still using the older HTTP protocol. Fast-forward to now, and Google is making good on that promise. The tech giant just confirmed that Chrome’s “Always Use Secure Connections” setting, which was enabled for users enrolled in Chrome’s Enhanced Protection mode of Safe Browsing earlier this year, has now become a standard part of the browsing experience.

title: Your YouTube feed might soon be free of fake Mr Beast x Elon Musk livestreams
summary: Channels suspected of being hacked will also be restricted from adding videos to playlists.
body: TL;DR YouTube has announced new security measures to protect channel owners if hackers take over their accounts. The platform says it won’t pause monetization for those accounts, but will impose other restrictions, such as preventing them from starting a livestream. YouTube will also give account owners the information they need on why their account was paused, along with next steps. Reports of social media accounts being hacked and held for ransom by criminals aren’t particularly new. Many YouTube channel owners have faced similar issues, including an official Google channel that fell prey to a crypto scam not too long ago . Now, YouTube is strengthening its defenses against such malicious actors by implementing some new safeguards. In a support page post , the streaming platform said it is temporarily pausing certain features for accounts when it notices “unusual activity.”

Access should be available now across the US, with a global rollout similarly in progress. Gemini continues its spread across everything Google touches . When it’s not coming to new apps, it’s coming to our smart home devices, and even our cars. While Gemini on Android Auto has resulted in a few (hilarious) rough patches, it’s getting better all the time. And now Gemini’s making new progress over on the Apple side of the fence, as Google finally brings Gemini in navigation to Google Maps on CarPlay. Considering how important it is to keep our interactions while driving as hands-free as possible, this is a big upgrade for CarPlay users. During navigation in Google Maps, users can talk to Gemini to find alternate routes, locate a place to refuel, or get advice about new destinations to add to the route.

body: If there’s one tech trend I can’t wait to see the back of this year, it’s the product name word salad. It’s Pro Max phones galore, with brands seemingly hoping that borrowing Apple’s naming formula will deliver the same success. When the new OPPO Find X10 Pro Max landed on my desk earlier this month, I was filled with dread that yet another brand was about to sacrifice its few remaining novelties at the altar of iPhone-sameness. Look past the naming vanity, though, and there’s a lot more Max-ing going on here than on any other phone sharing the moniker. A blazing-fast 2nm processor, gargantuan 7,150mAh battery, 80W charging, and not one but three huge 200-megapixel cameras . If numbers made great phones, the Find X10 Pro Max would already be a clear winner.

title: Silicon-carbon batteries have changed the game — Apple and Samsung need to catch up
summary: 5,000mAh batteries are starting to feel increasingly small.
body: Credit: Robert Triggs / Android Authority Smartphone battery capacity is undergoing a revolution at the moment, thanks to increasingly mainstream silicon-carbon battery technology found in high-end handsets. Even the notoriously slow Samsung has adopted it in its latest Galaxy Z Fold 8 series . What started out as a reasonably modest boost to 6,000 mAh capacities has quickly reached 8,000 mAh and even 10,000 mAh models, almost doubling battery capacity potential in just a few short years. I’ve had the new OPPO Find X10 Pro Max in my pocket for the past few weeks, itself sporting an 8,000mAh Si-C cell. Though I should note that global models ship with a slightly reduced 7,150mAh split-cell design. OPPO claims that both models are sufficient for two days of typical use, and I’ve put my handset through our testing wringer to find out just how much longer it can endure compared to rival flagships.

title: Forget custom ROMs, you can now run iOS on Android phones
summary: Not using emulation or a sandboxed environment. The real deal!
body: Credit: GitHub / ios-sweet TL;DR Some developers have figured out a way to run iOS on Android phones. The process involves spoofing an iPhone X’s device drivers and running a custom version of the iPhone’s XNU kernel. Many of the components don’t work, but we’re seeing efforts to make them usable, one by one. Most popular Android skins now tend to copy iOS in terms of aesthetics. But what about real, actual iOS running on Android devices? I thought I was dreaming when I first heard claims that developers were porting iOS to Android devices. But over the last couple of days, I’ve seen countless reports of Apple’s proprietary operating system booting on a range of Android devices. It’s part of a new movement called “Hackios,” inspired by the iconic Hackintosh, which runs macOS on non-Apple hardware. The idea comes from an enthusiast’s GitHub project called “ iow-sweet ,” which replaces Android’s stock Linux kernel with XNU, Apple’s custom kernel for iPhones and iPads. A kernel is the core program of any operating system that dictates how hardware interacts with the software running on it. Here’s a detailed explainer on kernels if you’d like to read one.

The developer is already moving forward with new projects, including Mornye for mobile and Stream Hoarder for desktop. Spotify may have finally embraced lossless audio for Premium subscribers, but some music lovers still prefer to keep their favorite tracks offline as actual files rather than relying on a streaming subscription. That’s where SpotiFLAC comes in. The third-party tool uses Spotify’s music catalog to help users find and download songs as lossless audio files from other streaming services. Unfortunately, Spotify’s legal team has now taken notice, forcing the developer to pull the project’s public GitHub repositories. However, the story doesn’t end there. The U2 Pro can track intruders as they move and even track cars going at up to 19 mph. We saw a handful of cool innovations from multiple brands during last month’s IFA 2026 . Prominent among them was Baseus, which unveiled the PrimeSentinel U2 Pro security camera with spotlight, featuring a motor that detects and illuminates the subject, even as they move. This unique outdoor security camera is now available in the US. The U2 Pro features a 3K camera at the top with a 130-degree field of view and 8x digital zoom. Below it is another 3K camera and floodlight with pan-and-tilt functions, thanks to the built-in motor (via TheVerge ). The camera at the top has a fixed focus, making it ideal for everyday security, but the second unit at the bottom is where all the magic happens.

We recently asked readers whether the practice affects their faith in Google’s services, and the results are in. While this Android phone verification has been in place for some time, it came to the fore when spotlighted in a much-upvoted Reddit post last week. Google automatically verifies your phone number and links it to every Google account signed in on your Android device, including secondary and work accounts, without explicitly asking for your permission. title: Chrome can now share your clipboard data with Google servers (for your own good)
summary: Google Chrome's scam protection is getting better — and more intrusive.
body: TL;DR Google Chrome is getting three new Enhanced Safe Browsing Protection features. It can share the webpages you visit with Safe Browsing servers to protect you from a broader range of scams. It can also share your clipboard content with Google’s servers to protect against social engineering scams like ClickFix. Google introduced Enhanced Protection in Chrome over half a decade ago. Since then, the company has added several new tools to identify increasingly sophisticated online threats and protect Chrome users from them. Now, Google is introducing three new features in Enhanced Safe Browsing Protection to combat web scams and further protect users. Google Chrome now takes a two-tiered approach to site safety warnings, displaying either a suspicious website pop-up or a full-screen dangerous site warning. When a Chrome user navigates to a website displaying known deceptive patterns, Chrome will show a new suspicious website pop-up informing the user that the site might not be safe.
